paragraphs: Image segmentation assigns a category to each pixel, so natural image corruptions can interfere with many closely connected decisions. This makes robustness especially challenging for perception systems operating outside controlled conditions. The paper tackles this problem by using sensitivity analysis to guide training augmentation: it estimates how input changes influence model outputs and uses that information to adapt the augmentation process.

The practical obstacle is that sensitivity analysis can itself demand substantial computation and storage. The proposed analysis runs about ten times faster on average and uses roughly two hundred times less storage than the previous sensitivity analysis considered. These savings make it practical to estimate sensitivities during training, supporting a model-free augmentation policy that responds to those estimates.

With minimal fine-tuning, the resulting method improves robustness on both real-world and synthetic datasets compared with leading segmentation augmentation techniques. The contribution connects cheaper analysis with better training decisions: sensitivity information becomes usable during learning, and the reported experiments show that this guidance helps segmentation models withstand natural corruptions.
icml-2025-adaptive-sensitivity-analysis-.tldr: Faster, lower-storage sensitivity analysis guides adaptive augmentation that improves image segmentation robustness against natural corruptions.

paragraphs: A language model can produce a correct-looking answer without reliably generating the reasoning needed to reach it. BRiTE addresses how to automatically obtain useful reasoning processes and then use them to improve the model. The paper introduces a probabilistic graphical model that connects hidden thinking processes with evaluation signals, providing a shared framework for inference and post-training.

The algorithm alternates between two steps. First, reinforcement learning with a new reward-shaping mechanism generates rationales by approximating a desired posterior distribution. In plain terms, it seeks reasoning processes favored by the probabilistic framework and its evaluation information. Second, it fine-tunes the base model by maximizing the joint probability associated with rationale generation.

The authors establish theoretical convergence at a rate of 1/T, where T counts iterations. On GSM8K and MATH, BRiTE consistently improves results across model sizes without human-annotated thinking processes. It outperforms standard chain-of-thought prompting and strengthens existing post-training methods, supporting the usefulness of repeatedly generating and learning from better rationales.
icml-2025-brite-bootstrapping-reinforced.tldr: BRiTE alternates reinforcement-based rationale generation with model fine-tuning to improve mathematical reasoning without human-annotated thinking processes.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning can treat decision trajectories as sequences and use transformers to model them. However, the useful context depends on the task: nearby features and longer-term dependencies do not always deserve equal attention. Modeling their interaction poorly can reduce performance while adding unnecessary computation. Decision Mixer addresses this balance through dynamic integration of information at different scales.

Its main component is a plug-and-play token selection mechanism inspired by conditional computation. The mechanism helps the model allocate attention according to task characteristics, adjusting which parts of the sequence contribute to its decisions. An auxiliary predictor separately addresses short-sighted behavior during autoregressive sampling, when decisions are generated sequentially.

The paper reports state-of-the-art performance on several standard reinforcement learning benchmarks while using substantially fewer computational resources. These findings support dynamic selection as a way to improve both decision quality and efficiency in the evaluated settings. The authors position the approach as a possible basis for more efficient, scalable reinforcement learning foundation models.
icml-2025-decision-mixer-integrating-lon.tldr: Decision Mixer dynamically selects sequence tokens to balance local and long-term information, improving benchmark performance with less computation.

paragraphs: Designing electromagnetic structures requires searching through many possible layouts, and evaluating each candidate can be expensive. Predictors and generators can reduce this burden, but training them often requires substantial data. Progressive Quadtree-based Search, or PQS, approaches the problem by changing how designs are represented and how the search spends its evaluation budget.

PQS converts an image-like layout into a hierarchical quadtree representation. This lets the search progress from broad structural patterns to finer local details instead of exploring the full design space exhaustively. A consistency-driven selection mechanism also estimates the reliability of predictions. It uses that information to balance refining promising candidates with exploring alternatives, reducing dependence on highly accurate predictors.

The authors evaluate PQS on dual-layer frequency selective surfaces and high-gain antennas. It produces satisfactory designs within limited computational budgets and outperforms the tested baselines. Compared with generative approaches, reported evaluation costs fall by 75–85%, corresponding to 20.27–38.80 days saved in the product design cycle. These results connect hierarchical search directly to practical engineering savings.
icml-2025-deep-electromagnetic-structure.tldr: PQS searches electromagnetic layouts from coarse structure to fine detail, reducing evaluation costs by 75–85% versus generative approaches in the reported tasks.

paragraphs: Traditional reinforcement learning from human feedback often evaluates an entire response with a single reward. This leaves learning algorithms with sparse information about which individual token choices contributed to response quality. The paper reformulates alignment as a Markov decision process, allowing decisions within a response to receive more detailed treatment than a sentence-level bandit formulation provides.

Reinforced Token Optimization, or RTO, learns token-wise rewards from preference data and uses those rewards to optimize the language model. Its practical implementation connects Direct Preference Optimization with Proximal Policy Optimization. Although DPO originates from a sentence-level reward formulation, the authors derive a token-wise characterization of quality from it and incorporate that signal into subsequent PPO training.

The paper provides theoretical support for the finer-grained formulation and establishes RTO's capability to find a near-optimal policy sample-efficiently. Experiments compare it with PPO and other direct preference learning algorithms. RTO exceeds PPO by 7.5 points on AlpacaEval 2 and 4.1 points on Arena-Hard, supporting the value of more detailed reward information in those evaluations.
icml-2025-dpo-meets-ppo-reinforced-token.tldr: RTO turns preference data into token-wise rewards through DPO and uses them in PPO to improve language-model alignment.

paragraphs: Masked language models learn by reconstructing hidden parts of an input from the remaining context. The paper examines a complication of this training setup: replacing content with mask tokens can leave a context that supports several competing meanings. Its analysis identifies this corrupted-semantics problem as a key influence on performance in downstream tasks.

ExLM addresses the ambiguity by expanding mask tokens into additional states and modeling dependencies among those states. This increases the capacity available to represent the incomplete context, allowing the model to capture richer semantic information during pre-training. The intervention changes how masked context is represented rather than simply treating every missing position as a single unchanged placeholder.

Experiments show significant improvements in both text modeling and SMILES modeling. Further analysis links the gains to richer semantic representations and reduced semantic multimodality, meaning fewer competing interpretations in the learned representations. The findings suggest that the representation of missing content is an important part of masked learning, with consequences for the usefulness of the resulting model.
icml-2025-exlm-rethinking-the-impact-of-.tldr: ExLM expands mask-token representations and models their dependencies to reduce semantic ambiguity and improve text and SMILES modeling.

paragraphs: Many reasoning benchmarks supply all the evidence needed to solve a problem. AR-Bench examines a different capability: recognizing that information is missing and interacting with an external system to obtain it. This separates reasoning over a complete prompt from active reasoning, where asking useful questions is part of solving the task.

The benchmark contains detective cases, situation puzzles, and number-guessing tasks. Together, these task families cover commonsense, logical, and symbolic reasoning in interactive settings. Success depends on both acquiring relevant information and making effective use of it, so the benchmark can expose failures that ordinary question-answering evaluations may overlook.

Evaluations find pronounced difficulties among contemporary language models, including failures to collect or use necessary evidence. Ablations show that tree-based search and post-training approaches provide only modest improvements, which the authors judge insufficient for real-world deployment. The results motivate further work on interactive learning, real-time feedback, and objectives that account for the environment; these are proposed directions rather than demonstrated solutions in the abstract.
icml-2025-from-passive-to-active-reasoni.tldr: AR-Bench reveals that language models struggle to ask for and use missing information, even when stronger search or post-training strategies are applied.

paragraphs: Autoregressive image models commonly predict a dense sequence of image tokens at a single scale. Early predictions have limited access to global context, even though they help determine the image's overall structure. Hi-MAR addresses this issue by organizing generation into a hierarchy that begins with a small number of low-resolution tokens.

In the first phase, the model predicts these coarse tokens as intermediary pivots that represent global structure. Later autoregressive phases use the pivots as additional guidance when modeling dense image tokens. This gives detailed predictions an explicit source of structural context. A new Diffusion Transformer head further strengthens global information exchange among tokens for masked-token prediction.

The authors evaluate Hi-MAR on both class-conditional generation and text-to-image generation. It outperforms the typical autoregressive baselines considered while requiring less computation. The results support a generation strategy in which a compact global representation guides subsequent detail, connecting improvements in image modeling with a more computationally efficient hierarchy.
icml-2025-hierarchical-masked-autoregres.tldr: Hi-MAR generates low-resolution token pivots to guide detailed image generation, outperforming typical autoregressive baselines with less computation.

paragraphs: Predicting properties of subgraphs requires representing groups of connected nodes whose sizes and connectivity can vary. Existing approaches can lose essential properties through simple pooling or depend on rigid definitions of what a subgraph must be. The paper also identifies inadequate modeling of long-range relationships within and across subgraphs as a significant weakness.

The proposed implicit subgraph neural network is designed to capture dependencies across subgraphs while incorporating label-aware information at the subgraph level. Its learning procedure is formulated as a bilevel optimization problem, linking two levels of optimization. This makes subgraph learning part of the model's optimization framework rather than relying only on a standard pooled graph representation.

The authors develop a provably convergent algorithm that uses fewer gradient estimations than standard bilevel optimization methods. Tests on real-world networks show stronger performance than the state-of-the-art baselines evaluated. The contribution therefore combines a richer approach to subgraph dependencies with an optimization procedure intended to make that learning more efficient.
icml-2025-implicit-subgraph-neural-netwo.tldr: An implicit subgraph network learns cross-subgraph dependencies through bilevel optimization with a provably convergent, gradient-efficient algorithm.

paragraphs: Diffusion and Flow Matching models can generate high-quality samples, but their inference procedures are slow. Converting them into models that sample in fewer steps can introduce unstable training and extensive tuning. Moment Matching Self-Distillation, or MMSD, proposes a class of generative models designed for one-step or few-step sampling through a single training stage.

MMSD avoids the pre-trained initialization and two-network optimization required by the distillation setup discussed in the paper. The authors also establish convergence at the distribution level, a guarantee concerning the generated distribution. They report stable behavior across various hyperparameters and standard model architectures, addressing another source of difficulty in training efficient generators.

On ImageNet at 256 by 256 resolution, MMSD achieves an FID of 2.13 using eight inference steps, surpassing diffusion models in the reported comparison. A model trained from scratch reaches a state-of-the-art two-step FID of 2.05 on CIFAR-10. These findings support the proposed combination of a simpler training pipeline, few-step generation, and strong measured sample quality.
icml-2025-inductive-moment-matching-b7fb.tldr: MMSD trains one-step or few-step generators in a single stage, with distribution-level convergence guarantees and strong reported image-generation results.

paragraphs: Inverse problems reconstruct an underlying signal from noisy observations. Diffusion models provide a useful framework for this reconstruction, but existing solvers can require substantial computation and converge to suboptimal solutions. Building on DMPlug, the paper introduces DMILO and DMILO-PGD to improve the practicality and effectiveness of diffusion-based reconstruction.

DMILO uses intermediate layer optimization to reduce DMPlug's memory burden. It also introduces sparse deviations that expand the range of signals accessible through the model. This matters when the underlying signal lies outside the diffusion model's original range: reconstruction gains some flexibility to explore beyond what the unmodified model can represent.

DMILO-PGD combines intermediate layer optimization with projected gradient descent to reduce the risk of suboptimal convergence. The paper provides intuitive theoretical analysis under appropriate conditions and evaluates both methods across diverse image datasets with linear and nonlinear inverse problems. The reported gains over state-of-the-art methods support addressing memory demands, representational restrictions, and optimization behavior together, while the theoretical conclusions remain conditional.
icml-2025-integrating-intermediate-layer.tldr: DMILO and DMILO-PGD improve diffusion-based inverse-problem solving through intermediate-layer optimization, sparse deviations, and projected gradient descent.

paragraphs: Learning how a system evolves becomes harder when environmental constraints are known only through local, uncertain measurements. Methods that require globally available constraints may not suit this setting. The paper develops a geometric framework that connects measurements, constraints, and dynamics learning through a fiber bundle over the system's state space.

This structure organizes local measurement and constraint information in relation to system states. It supports measurement-aware Control Barrier Functions that adapt to sensing conditions. The framework then incorporates Neural ODEs to learn continuous-time dynamics while preserving geometric constraints, linking the learned motion of the system with the restrictions expressed by the geometry.

The authors provide theoretical guarantees for learning convergence and constraint satisfaction that depend on sensing quality. Simulations show substantial improvements in learning efficiency and constraint satisfaction over traditional methods, especially when sensing is limited or uncertain. The paper also suggests possible integration with reinforcement learning, but presents that connection as a promising direction rather than an established experimental result.
icml-2025-learning-dynamics-under-enviro.tldr: A geometric framework combines local sensing, constraint-aware control, and Neural ODEs to learn dynamics with guarantees dependent on sensing quality.

paragraphs: An agent operating in an open world must handle many different tasks, making evaluation difficult to scale. Minecraft Universe, or MCU, addresses this problem with an evaluation framework inside Minecraft. Its purpose is to test agents across a growing range of challenges instead of relying on a small, fixed task collection.

MCU starts with 3,452 composable atomic tasks organized into 11 major categories and 41 subcategories. A composition mechanism combines these building blocks into an unlimited variety of tasks with different difficulty levels. A general assessment framework evaluates open-ended performance and achieves 91.5% alignment with human ratings in the reported evaluation.

Experiments show that even state-of-the-art foundation agents struggle as task diversity and complexity increase. This makes the compositional design consequential: it exposes weaknesses that emerge when agents face a broader and more demanding task space. MCU contributes both a scalable way to construct evaluations and evidence that current agents remain challenged by the open-ended capabilities it measures.
icml-2025-mcu-an-evaluation-framework-fo.tldr: MCU composes thousands of Minecraft task building blocks into diverse evaluations that reveal weaknesses in current open-world agents.

paragraphs: Heuristics help solve complex optimization problems, but designing them manually requires considerable domain expertise. Language models offer a way to generate heuristics automatically. Existing approaches often keep a fixed population of top-performing candidates and improve them through evolutionary computation, which can leave promising alternatives underdeveloped and encourage convergence to local optima.

MCTS-AHD replaces this population-centered search with Monte Carlo Tree Search. It organizes generated heuristics into a tree, providing a structure for exploring their evolution. A central motivation is that a heuristic performing poorly now may still lead to a useful descendant. The tree-based approach can continue developing such candidates rather than focusing exclusively on current top performers.

Across experiments on several complex tasks, MCTS-AHD produces significantly higher-quality heuristics. The findings support broader exploration of the heuristic space as a useful complement to language-model generation. The contribution is principally a change in how candidate heuristics are organized and explored, allowing the search to better investigate potential that immediate performance alone may not reveal.
icml-2025-monte-carlo-tree-search-for-co.tldr: MCTS-AHD uses tree search to develop language-model-generated heuristics, including temporarily weak candidates, and finds better heuristics in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: A neural network can learn to associate a class with an incidental feature, such as a background that frequently accompanies an object. Predictions then deteriorate when that association disappears. NeuronTune addresses these spurious correlations without requiring annotations that explicitly identify them, which can be difficult to obtain and may not match the biases a particular model has learned.

The method operates after training and intervenes directly in the model's internal decision process. It probes the latent embedding space to identify neurons associated with spurious prediction behavior, then regulates those neurons. This makes the model's own behavior the basis for intervention rather than depending on externally supplied descriptions of its shortcuts.

The authors theoretically justify the approach and show that it moves the model closer to an unbiased one. Experiments across multiple architectures and data modalities demonstrate significant mitigation of spurious bias. These findings support self-guided internal intervention as a practical route toward greater robustness, while the stated result is bias reduction rather than complete elimination.
icml-2025-neurontune-towards-self-guided.tldr: NeuronTune probes and regulates internal neurons to reduce spurious prediction behavior without annotations of the spurious correlations.

paragraphs: Concept learning aims to recover the hidden concepts that explain observations. Strong empirical performance alone does not establish whether those recovered concepts correspond to the underlying ones. This paper develops an identifiability framework based on comparing multiple classes of observations, asking when such comparisons provide enough information to recover latent concepts.

The main result requires sufficient diversity across observation classes. Under that condition, concepts can be identified without specifying their types, the functional relationships involved, or a parametric model for generating the data. The significance is that the guarantee rests on informative variation across classes rather than a narrowly prescribed form for the hidden concepts.

The theory also addresses cases where its conditions do not hold globally. Local comparisons can provide alternative guarantees for as many concepts as possible, extending identification to more flexible settings. The authors additionally show that the hidden relationships between classes and concepts can be identified nonparametrically. Synthetic and real-world evaluations support the theoretical results, connecting the comparison-based framework with observed data.
icml-2025-nonparametric-identification-o.tldr: Sufficient diversity across observation classes enables nonparametric identification of hidden concepts, with local guarantees when global conditions fail.

paragraphs: Mixture-of-Experts models activate only a few experts for each token, suggesting that inference could fit within limited memory. In practice, consecutive tokens may activate different experts so frequently that moving experts in and out of memory dominates latency. Oracle-MoE targets this temporal inconsistency in expert activation.

Its routing mechanism places tokens in a compact representation called the oracle space, derived from attention scores. Routing in this space preserves semantic locality across consecutive tokens, reducing changes in which experts are activated and therefore reducing swapping demands. The paper provides theoretical analysis supporting better semantic locality in routing decisions and improved consistency of expert activation.

Experiments use pretrained GPT-2 architectures at 200M, 350M, 790M, and 2B parameter scales, along with downstream tasks. Across varying memory budgets, Oracle-MoE achieves state-of-the-art inference speeds without compromising task performance in the reported evaluations. The result connects routing behavior to a practical deployment bottleneck: sparse activation helps memory-constrained inference most when the active experts also remain sufficiently consistent over time.
icml-2025-oracle-moe-locality-preserving.tldr: Oracle-MoE improves routing consistency across consecutive tokens to reduce expert swapping and accelerate memory-constrained inference.

paragraphs: Personalizing a soft exosuit's walking assistance requires adapting a physical controller while managing limited data, real-time computation, and human safety. The paper addresses this setting without a simulator of human-robot walking interactions. Its Adaptation from an offline Imitating Expert Policy approach, or AIP, combines an offline starting policy with online reinforcement learning.

Offline learning imitates human expert actions using demonstrations of real walking without robot assistance. That learned policy initializes an online actor-critic procedure, which adapts assistance to the individual. This sequence gives online personalization an initial policy derived from demonstrations while reserving further learning for interaction with the physical device.

The authors report properties including learning convergence, dynamic stability, and solution optimality for their online method. They demonstrate safe robot control on all five tested participants and explicitly report the full tested group. Together, the qualitative guarantees and consistent participant results provide evidence for online personalization of softsuit control; the physical validation described covers those five participants.
icml-2025-reinforcement-learning-control.tldr: AIP initializes soft-exosuit control from walking demonstrations and personalizes assistance through online reinforcement learning, with successful tests on five participants.

paragraphs: Diffusion distillation reduces sampling steps but can require extensive training and weaken the resulting student. This paper identifies a mismatch between teacher and student step sizes and parameter counts: they can converge to different local minima, making direct imitation suboptimal. The authors investigate whether adversarial training can avoid this obstacle.

They demonstrate that a standalone GAN objective, without a distillation loss, is sufficient to convert diffusion models into one-step generators in their setting. This supports viewing diffusion training as generative pre-training whose capabilities can be accessed through lightweight GAN fine-tuning. The proposal changes the role of the pretrained model from an imitation target to a foundation for further generative training.

The authors fine-tune a pretrained model while freezing 85% of its parameters, reporting strong performance with 0.2 million images and near-state-of-the-art results with 5 million. A frequency-domain analysis offers a possible explanation for the one-step capabilities acquired during diffusion training. That explanation is presented as suggestive, while the generation results provide empirical support for the pre-training perspective.
icml-2025-revisiting-diffusion-models-fr.tldr: GAN fine-tuning can convert pretrained diffusion models into one-step generators without a distillation loss, even with most parameters frozen.

paragraphs: Dataset distillation compresses a large training dataset into a small synthetic subset while aiming to preserve model performance. However, models trained on distilled data can remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks. ROME targets this robustness problem using the information bottleneck principle, extending the objective beyond retaining ordinary predictive accuracy.

The method combines two terms with different roles. A performance-aligned term preserves accuracy, while a robustness-aligned term brings the feature distributions of synthetic images and perturbed images into alignment. This explicitly connects dataset construction to how the resulting representations respond to perturbations. The authors also introduce the Improved Robustness Ratio, or I-RR, to refine evaluation of robustness in dataset distillation.

Experiments on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 show that ROME improves adversarial robustness over existing distillation methods. Maximum reported I-RR improvements approach 40% under white-box attacks and 35% under black-box attacks. These are peak improvements in the proposed metric, supporting the method's effectiveness in the tested attack settings without implying uniform gains across every experiment.
icml-2025-rome-is-forged-in-adversity-ro.tldr: ROME combines accuracy preservation with feature-distribution alignment to improve adversarial robustness of models trained on distilled datasets.

paragraphs: CPL-IQA addresses image quality assessment when labeled examples are limited and images contain authentic distortions. Its semi-supervised approach uses unlabeled images through pseudo-labels, while learning how much confidence to place in those labels. This targets a central difficulty of the setting: automatically assigned training targets can be unreliable.

The framework first converts MOS labels into vector labels through entropy minimization. It then alternates model training with label optimization, allowing the prediction model and its training labels to be refined iteratively. Label optimization relies on a manifold assumption, and a separate confidence-learning method estimates pseudo-label reliability. Together, these components are designed to reduce the influence of outliers.

Experiments on datasets of real-world distorted images show superior performance. The authors report these gains without additional supervision or increased network complexity. The contribution therefore lies in organizing and assessing the available training information more effectively: unlabeled examples contribute through targets whose reliability is explicitly considered, rather than being treated as equally trustworthy.
icml-2025-semi-supervised-blind-quality-.tldr: CPL-IQA improves semi-supervised image quality assessment by iteratively refining pseudo-labels and learning their confidence.

paragraphs: In multi-view multi-label classification, an object has several different feature views and may belong to multiple labels. A useful model must capture both agreement across views and relationships among labels. The paper argues that handling these with independent components overlooks their interactions, and proposes TMvML to represent them jointly.

TMvML reorganizes the mapping matrices used for classification into a tensor classifier. It rotates this tensor and imposes a low-rank constraint to encourage feature consistency across views alongside semantic co-occurrence among labels. The shared tensor representation lets these two kinds of structure influence the same classifier rather than being addressed in separate components.

The authors introduce Laplace Tensor Rank as a tighter surrogate for tensor rank, intended to capture higher-order correlations among tensor fibers. This provides a concise constraint for extracting view and label relationships together. Extensive experiments show significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods, supporting the value of jointly modeling these interacting structures within the evaluated multi-view, multi-label classification problems.
icml-2025-tensorized-multi-view-multi-la.tldr: TMvML uses a low-rank tensor classifier to jointly capture consistency across feature views and relationships among multiple labels.

paragraphs: Time-series forecasting can benefit from descriptions and visual representations, but each supplies different information. Text offers semantic context while potentially missing fine temporal detail; visual representations capture intricate temporal patterns but may lack contextual meaning. Time-VLM combines temporal, visual, and textual information through pretrained vision-language models.

The framework contains three cooperating components. A retrieval-augmented learner enriches temporal features through interactions with a memory bank. A vision-augmented learner encodes the time series as informative images, while a text-augmented learner produces contextual descriptions. Frozen pretrained vision-language models turn these inputs into multimodal embeddings, which are fused with temporal features for the final forecast.

Experiments report superior forecasting performance, particularly in few-shot and zero-shot scenarios. These findings support combining complementary representations while keeping the pretrained vision-language models frozen. The distinctive contribution is the coordinated pipeline: retrieval supplies enriched temporal information, and visual and textual processing contribute additional representations that are brought together at prediction time.
icml-2025-time-vlm-exploring-multimodal-.tldr: Time-VLM combines retrieved temporal features, time-series images, and textual descriptions through frozen vision-language models to improve forecasting.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks perform well at node classification, but gathering multi-hop information during inference can make them costly in latency-sensitive applications. TINED transfers their knowledge into multilayer perceptrons through a layer-by-layer process. It focuses on the internal operations of the teacher rather than relying only on its final predictions.

The method separates feature transformation from graph propagation. Because feature transformation is computationally equivalent to an MLP's fully connected layer, TINED directly transfers those teacher parameters and then fine-tunes them. Student layers follow the sequence of transformation and propagation operations, and the paper establishes a theoretical bound for approximating graph propagation.

TINED also transfers smoothing behavior. The authors observe that propagation is often aggressively smoothing while feature transformation is more conservative. They use a Dirichlet-energy ratio to measure these effects and distill them into student layers. Across seven datasets and multiple settings, TINED outperforms both GNNs and leading distillation methods, supporting the value of preserving layer-level operations and representation characteristics.
icml-2025-tined-gnns-to-mlps-by-teacher-.tldr: TINED distills GNNs into MLPs by transferring transformation parameters and layer-level smoothing behavior, improving results across seven datasets.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks can struggle when training nodes and test nodes come from different distributions. Existing remedies include invariant learning and sample reweighting. The paper identifies problems with both: invariant approaches may depend on unavailable environment labels and overly strict invariance, while reweighting approaches can overlook the graph's connectivity.

Topology-Aware Dynamic Reweighting, or TAR, uses graph structure to adjust sample weights during training. Its updates follow gradient flow on graph edges, making connectivity part of how training influence is redistributed. This connects reweighting to the relationships among nodes instead of treating the samples as an unstructured collection.

The authors theoretically establish that TAR can provide distributional robustness without relying on strict invariance assumptions. Evaluations across extensive out-of-distribution node classification datasets show marked improvements over existing methods. The contribution is therefore both structural and practical: it uses information already present in the graph to guide training weights, and the reported results support that choice under the tested distribution shifts.
icml-2025-topology-aware-dynamic-reweigh.tldr: TAR dynamically reweights training samples using graph edges to improve node classification under distribution shifts.
